title: Git clone 'Filename too long' across projects
story: A clinic entry covers long clone paths and a second DLL half. A FixFlow top-model session hit 15 of 15 clone failures. It fixed them inline. The clinic entry is not in the FixFlow store.
entry: Windows: git clone fails 'Filename too long' when the destination root is long. Fix per command: git clone -c core.longpaths=true. Limit: longpaths fixes git only. Native Python modules then fail 'DLL load failed ... filename or extension is too long'. Keep the root under about 100 characters.
worked: The memory index pushed the fix to sibling sessions, and one later session used the flag on its first clone with zero failures.
steps: The main session was on the top tier, not a cheap model. 15 of 15 clone errors were in the persisted output.
A research-script clone is not a listed trigger. Fable fixed it inline with no rung above. No lookup.
The text 'unable to open loose object: Filename too long' differs from the stored 'cannot create directory'. Only 'Filename too long' overlaps.
The store is one FixFlow store with a FixFlow seed. The clinic entry is not there. Cross-project matching is not specified.
The main session held it. No compaction came before the note was written.
One flag. The DLL half is irrelevant to markdown clones and harmless.
Re-running the clone is the real check. No check kind reads a machine path length, so 'applies' is unreachable and the fix text is withheld.
The git half fixed on the first retry is below the write bar. The DLL half qualifies but its cause is the clone root, not a commit. FixFlow's writer stored only the git half.
The memory index pushed the fix to siblings. A pull-only lookup would not have fired there. The DLL rule never reached FixFlow.

title: Subagents blocked from writing report files
story: Two clinic subagents could not write report files. A FixFlow correction said 'They can'. Next day eight of eight report.md writes were refused, 187,160 characters in all.
entry: Two Opus subagents could not write their report files and returned the text instead. Sonnet extractors in the same session wrote .md outputs. Cause not isolated (agent type? output size?). Workaround: brief subagents to return the full result; the parent saves it.
steps: One was a Fable session verifying the owner's list. Others were subagents whose brief says 'Put a full report.md there'.
Checking a claim raises no error. At the subagent the harness message itself says to return text. The window that needed the entry was the Fable writing the brief, and nothing triggers at brief time.
Paraphrase matches paraphrase. The exact harness string matches nothing, because no entry ever stored it.
The top result would be FixFlow's 11-11 correction 'They can', the opposite of what had just happened to 8 agents.
The design reads by the escalating session. How a workflow subagent's one-shot window receives an entry is not stated.
The correction was used. 8 of 8 report.md writes were refused, 187,160 characters.
A probe wrote a .txt in bypass mode. The original refusals were analysis-*.md. A check at a different scope 'refuted' an entry right for its own scope.
No climb. The refusals were absorbed as returned text.
The root saw only the subagent's paraphrase. The raw error naming 'report files' stayed in subagent transcripts, which the design forbids extracting.
A hedge, then a flat rule, then a paste to FixFlow, then 'They can', then 8 refusals next day. A document edited at 08:07Z still says 'They can'. Nothing links refusals back to the refutation.

title: Explore subagent inherits the top tier
story: A FixFlow rule says route every agent explicitly. The clinic root started three sessions with no model. Only the owner's message surfaced it. The rule reached neither the new tool nor FixFlow's own calls.
entry: The built-in Explore subagent runs on the session's model, so from a Fable session a 'where is X?' search runs on Fable. Use the project agent fixflow-explorer (model: haiku, read-only) for file location. Route every agent explicitly; cheap work must not inherit the top tier.
steps: The clinic root was Fable 5.1 with about 460k cached tokens. The FixFlow rule was in the window at line 3. The actor is the top-tier orchestrator.
start_session with no model raises no error. No trigger fires on a session start. Three starts without a model, and only the owner's message surfaced it.
The stored action is a subagent type for search. The act is a session start. No shared verb or object.
A meaning-level match returns a fix, pin an agent file to Haiku, that does not apply to start_session. Only the principle carries, stated for one tool.
It was already in the main window.
The rule was present and not carried to the neighbouring tool, three times.
No check decides 'right tier'. The output would be correct, only dearer. The owner's eye was the check.
The actor is the top rung and the failure is overspend. The ladder climbs on failure and does not see it.
Write-through worked. Memory was edited within 30 seconds and a commit followed seven minutes later. The note bundles five facts of different scope, and no check kind fits a session parameter.
It never reached FixFlow, where 7 of 7 start_session calls pass no model. No objection was recorded. A crossed rule cannot tell intended from mistaken.

title: Clinic checks: Linux container allowed here
source: Session e24f17dc; HARNESS-BOTTLENECKS line 65; owner decision USER-23
story: The clinic measured its full check as latency-bound and moved tests to a Linux container. In FixFlow a Fable session chose a workaround and wrote a limit instead. The owner was the escalation.
entry: Clinic full check on Windows is latency-bound, not CPU-bound. Pytest in a Linux container beside Postgres: 230.1 s vs 367.2 s native. Owner decision USER-23: tests go to a Linux container next to the database. Measure before serialising.
steps: A Fable 5.2 session with about 380k cached tokens held the library import list and its own 230 s Linux line.
The model did not fail. It chose a workaround and a written limit. No trigger fires on 'about to record a handicap'.
'function page_rank is not defined' and the arrow and networkit DLL names share no word with the clinic entry.
Similar, not the same. The clinic entry is about speed. This is a missing native library. What carries is a permission, 'Linux is approved here', not a solution.
The real work was new: libssl3, libgomp1, Arrow 26 and icebug 13.5. Nothing in the clinic entry carries it.
'Extension: all libraries resolved' and a PageRank result are mechanical checks, though outside any check kind.
The owner was the escalation. Accepting a handicap is not a failure any check sees.
The correction was stored as a memory preference and the recipe as a Dockerfile in evidence. Neither passes the write gate.

The recipe pins versions outside any repo lockfile. Invalidation cannot see untracked dependencies. Two stored rules now collide: no installs without an owner decision, and Docker/Linux already approved.

title: Long Bash heredoc from a subagent
story: A long Bash command failed with ENAMETOOLONG in one agent and 'unexpected EOF' in another. The clinic stored the fact only inside a subagent-write note. The rule's own author sent an 8,720-character call 25 hours later.
entry: A long Bash heredoc from a subagent failed: ENAMETOOLONG name too long, and in another agent 'unexpected EOF while looking for matching'. Split long writes into parts. (The clinic stored only 'one also failed a long Bash heredoc' inside the subagent-write note.)
steps: A Fable 5.2 main session had the 8 KB rule in its index, its compaction summary and its own subagent briefs.
Writing a long command is not an error until it fails. Then the cost is one failed call.
The EOF line is a clean template, identical to the clinic's. Nothing stored carries it.
In the clinic the symptom is bundled in the subagent-write note, so a hit returns the wrong fact. The FixFlow store does not hold clinic entries.
It was already delivered inside FixFlow.
The rule's own author sent an 8,720-character Bash call 25 hours after writing it.
A rerun is the check. No check kind covers the shell.
The clinic bundled two facts in one note without the error strings. FixFlow re-derived the second fact on 11-11.
Only in-project push reached later windows. Nothing crossed projects.
